subject: Logic
title: Schrödinger's Cat
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Schrödinger's Cat.

hook.text: A cat in a sealed box is simultaneously alive and dead—until you open the lid. That's quantum mechanics talking.

buildup.text: Schrödinger designed this in 1935 not to celebrate quantum weirdness but to show how absurd it sounds at human scale.

discovery.text: In quantum theory, particles exist in superposition—multiple states at once—until measured.

twist.text: Schrödinger thought this was a problem, not a feature. His cat was a reductio ad absurdum of the theory.

climax.text: Decades later, physicists embraced superposition as real. The cat was meant as criticism but became an icon.

punchline.text: The cat was a joke. Physics wasn't laughing.

quiz.question: Why did Schrödinger propose his cat experiment?
options: To show the absurdity of applying quantum superposition to everyday objects
